summary: UpsertBatchWithFacts (internal/store/peloton.go), for resourceType=="classes" only, routes incoming items through mergeClassesListItemsWithStoredDetail before the normal write. For each incoming item that is list-shaped (no top-level "ride" object -- the same signal classIsListForm/nestedIDContainerKeys use elsewhere), it looks up the currently-stored record for that id and, if that stored record IS detail-shaped, copies over every top-level key the incoming item lacks (not a fixed allowlist -- so a future detail-response field like a new provider metadata block survives automatically). A detail-shaped incoming item, or an id with no prior detail-shaped record, is returned completely unchanged: this only ever adds fields back, never removes or overrides anything the incoming (fresher) item already carries. Both the generic resources write and provider_payloads (recordProviderFactsBestEffort, called on the same merged `items` slice) get the merged shape, since planClassDetailSync's pending-check reads provider_payloads. Any future write path for "classes" that bypasses UpsertBatchWithFacts (a hand-rolled upsert, a new bulk endpoint) must route through this same merge or reintroduce the clobber.
reason: Round-12 live verification NEW A, marked as the fix that matters most: a real account's synced-classes-with-segments count went 187 -> 156 across a single `workflow archive` call. The flat classes phase's bulk catalog list endpoint re-fetched 500 catalog entries as list-shaped items and wholesale-overwrote the merged records classes_detail (see classes-detail-dependent-sync.json) had previously enriched, stripping segments/target_metrics_data from ~55 classes; classes_detail then re-added 24 in the same run, netting a loss. Without this fix, classes_detail's entire backfill oscillates rather than accumulates on any account that runs `sync --resources workouts,classes` or `workflow archive` routinely -- which is exactly the normal, expected usage pattern, not an edge case.
validated_outcome: go build/vet/test/govulncheck and verify_skill.py all green. TestUpsertBatchWithFacts_ClassesFlatSyncPreservesDetailFields seeds a detail-enriched class (segments, target_metrics_data, ride), then re-syncs it in list form with a different title, and asserts: the title updates to the fresher list-sync value, segments/target_metrics_data/ride all survive in BOTH the resources table and provider_payloads. TestUpsertBatchWithFacts_ClassesFlatSyncOfNeverDetailFetchedClassIsUnaffected asserts the common case (a class that was only ever synced in list form) is a complete no-op for the merge logic -- no extra fields appear, confirming the fix doesn't do anything for the vast majority of the catalog.
